{{Short description|American statistician and statistics educator}}
'''Deborah Jean Rumsey-Johnson''' (born 1961){{r|born}} is an American [[statistician]] and [[statistics education|statistics educator]]. She is an associated professor and program specialist in statistics at the [[Ohio State University]].{{r|osu}}

==Education and career==
Rumsey earned her Ph.D. at Ohio State in 1993. Her dissertation, ''Nonresponse in Social Network Analysis'', was supervised by [[Elizabeth Stasny]].{{r|mg}} 
In 2002 she became founding director of the Consortium for the Advancement of Undergraduate Statistics Education.{{r|cause}} She directed the Mathematics and Statistics Learning Center at Ohio State from 2000 to 2004,{{r|mslc}} and became a faculty member in the Ohio State Department of Statistics in 2004.{{r|osu|mslc}}

==Contributions==
Rumsey is the author of five books on statistics in the "[[For Dummies]]" book series.{{r|osu}} She is also the author of highly cited research publications on the statistics of people seeking employment,<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Wanberg | first1 = Connie R.
 | last2 = Watt | first2 = John D.
 | last3 = Rumsey | first3 = Deborah J.
 | doi = 10.1037/0021-9010.81.1.76
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Applied Psychology
 | pages = 76–87
 | title = Individuals without jobs: An empirical study of job-seeking behavior and reemployment.
 | volume = 81
 | year = 1996}}</ref> and on education for [[statistical literacy]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Rumsey | first = Deborah J.
 | date = January 2002
 | doi = 10.1080/10691898.2002.11910678
 | issue = 3
 | journal = Journal of Statistics Education
 | title = Statistical Literacy as a Goal for Introductory Statistics Courses
 | volume = 10| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Rumsey was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2006.{{r|fasa}}
